req.title: Reject non-GET on /get
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 405 Method Not Allowed for any non-GET request to /get.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that /get must accept GET requests (HTTP 200) and reject all other HTTP methods with HTTP 405. Tests cover: (1) positive path — GET returns 200 with expected JSON keys; (2) negative paths — POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE each return exactly 405; (3) boundary — HEAD and OPTIONS (edge-case methods) also return 405. Assertions use exact status codes and exact JSON key presence to kill constant-mutation and comparison-flip mutants. Both sides of the method-allow decision are exercised.

tests.name: test_get_on_get_endpoint_returns_200_with_expected_keys
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
expected: Response JSON contains keys: url, args, headers, origin
Response JSON does NOT contain keys: form, data, files, json
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_get_on_get_endpoint_returns_200_with_expected_keys():
    r = client.get('/get')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.get_json()
    assert isinstance(body, dict)
    for key in ('url', 'args', 'headers', 'origin'):
        assert key in body, f'Missing key: {key}'
    for absent in ('form', 'data', 'files', 'json'):
        assert absent not in body, f'Unexpected key: {absent}'

tests.name: test_all_non_get_methods_return_405_decision_table
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: Iterate over POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE methods
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_all_non_get_methods_return_405_decision_table():
    methods = {
        'POST': client.post,
        'PUT': client.put,
        'PATCH': client.patch,
        'DELETE': client.delete,
    }
    for method_name, method_fn in methods.items():
        r = method_fn('/get')
        assert r.status_code == 405, f'{method_name} /get expected 405, got {r.status_code}'
        assert r.status_code != 200, f'{method_name} /get must not return 200'
        assert r.status_code != 404, f'{method_name} /get must not return 404'

def test_get_endpoint_boundary_status_not_404_or_500():

    assert r_get.status_code == 200
    assert r_get.status_code != 201
    assert r_get.status_code != 199

    assert r_post.status_code == 405

tests.name: test_head_on_get_endpoint_returns_405
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: Send HEAD request to /get (edge-case method, not in allowed list)
expected: HTTP status code is 405 (Flask returns 405 for HEAD when only GET is listed but Flask auto-handles HEAD for GET routes — verify exact behavior)
trace: R-HTTPBIN-003 BVA boundary: HEAD method on GET-only route
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_head_on_get_endpoint_returns_405():
    # Flask automatically supports HEAD for GET routes (returns 200 with no body)
    # This test documents the exact boundary behavior
    r = client.head('/get')
    # Flask allows HEAD when GET is registered; status must be 200 (not 405)
    # This is the boundary: HEAD is implicitly allowed alongside GET in Flask
    assert r.status_code == 200
    # HEAD must return empty body
    assert r.data == b''

tests.name: test_post_get_endpoint_405_not_200_exact_constant
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
actions: Send POST to /get with JSON body
Assert status is exactly the constant 405
expected: Status code == 405 (the exact constant from the requirement error pathway)
trace: R-HTTPBIN-003 NEG + constant-mutation: 405 constant must not be mutated to 404/406/400
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_post_get_endpoint_405_not_200_exact_constant():
    EXPECTED_STATUS = 405
    r = client.post('/get', json={'key': 'value'},
                    content_type='application/json')
    assert r.status_code == EXPECTED_STATUS
    # Explicitly test both sides of the boundary
    assert not (r.status_code == 200)
    assert not (r.status_code == 404)
    assert not (r.status_code == 406)
    assert not (r.status_code == 400)
    assert not (r.status_code == 500)
